articles.description:
Communications
  
Ready for a little spring sunshine in your inbox? At Smily, we have been busy finding new ways to make your vacation rental world a bit brighter and your load a bit lighter. Because, let's face it, who doesn't love easier days and happier guests? 
Discover in this newsletter edition some tips to boost your revenue, improve your efficiency, and our latest news ☺️
🆕 Smily updates you don't want to miss!
New synchronized rule with Booking.com: Our rate rule "Reserve at least one x/day in advance" is now synced with Booking.com! 
Manage Vrbo reviews from Smily's interface: Collect and respond to Vrbo traveler's reviews directly from your Smily's account. Save time by using our AI-powered response feature!
Introducing simplified monthly billing: All new rental charges are now…
articles.title: Spring into success: Elevate your vacation rental business with Smily's latest innovations & news!

articles.author: Megan, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
 
Improvement
  
We're thrilled to announce an important update to our monthly billing process, driven by your valuable feedback. 🙌
We understand that receiving multiple invoices for your Smily subscription throughout the month has been an accounting headache for some of our customers. Therefore, we've made changes to streamline our billing process and improve your experience.
Starting immediately, all charges for new rentals will be consolidated onto one invoice, which will be issued on your account renewal date. This means that you will no longer receive separate invoices for each new rental added to your Smily account.
What does this mean for you?
📃 Consolidated Invoicing: on your account renewal date, you will receive an invoice for your Smily subscription for the upcoming month…
articles.title: Introducing Simplified Monthly Invoicing: All Rental Additions Unified on a Single Invoice

Mar 21, 18:15 UTC
Scheduled - Start Time: March 26 17:00 UTC
End Time: March 26 18:00 UTC
During this time, our Engineering Team will be performing maintenance to failover an internal service from one cluster to another. 
This maintenance has been previously conducted with limited impact and our team has done extensive planning and testing to ensure a smooth failover, with the least disruption possible.
Existing infrastructure (including Droplet and Droplet-based services networking) will continue running without issue. 
If the failover period lasts longer than expected, there may be customer impacts with associated services including: 
Droplet creates with a root password
Droplet root password resets 
MongoDB cluster creates 
Let’sEncrypt certificate creation (for Load Balancers and Spaces)
LoadBalancer creation with certificates
Spaces key creation
Marketplace (Add-Ons) will be unavailable for both vendors and users
App Platform builds and deploys may see latency 
Users will be unable to fetch CSV invoices 
Bulk actions in the Spaces UI
At this time, we do not expect to see any of the above listed impacts during maintenance, but are prepared for the worst case if needed.
If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to the Support team from within your account.
articles.title: Core Infrastructure Maintenance

During the above maintenance window, there will be maintenance performed on our ticketing system.
Expected Impact:
During the course of the maintenance, users will be unable to submit support tickets, update existing tickets, or receive replies to existing tickets. Users will also be unable to log into https://cloudsupport.digitalocean.com/s/ or open the Support Portal from within the Cloud Control Panel.
Any tickets submitted during the maintenance via alternate methods (such as replying to an email chain or via our webform) will be saved and entered into our ticketing system at the completion of the maintenance.
Our Support Team will also be impacted by this maintenance and will be unable to enter the ticketing system to receive any tickets or reply to existing tickets. As soon as the vendor maintenance has completed, our team will address all support queries as quickly as possible.
We appreciate your patience throughout this process.

articles.description:
Incident began at 2024-03-06 22:32 and ended at 2024-03-06 23:29 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Incident Report

Summary

On Wednesday, 06 March 2024, Google Workspace users experienced elevated errors while accessing user or device setting pages within the Chrome Admin Console for a duration of 1 hour, 27 minutes.

To our Google Workspace customers who were impacted during this disruption, we sincerely apologize. This is not the level of quality and reliability we strive to offer you, and we are taking immediate steps to improve the platform’s performance and availability.

Root Cause

Google Workspace Admin Console uses a backend authentication service to grant privileged access to internal accounts. As part of ongoing efforts to migrate the account authorization workflow to a new backend authentication service, Google engineers identified and cleaned up invalid account role assignments in the configuration.

During this clean up effort, engineers identified a privilege which was undefined in the application manifest and removed it from the configuration. Upon further investigation, engineering confirmed the privilege was mapped to an access control setting used by the Admin Console for Chrome. This change resulted in users being unable to access Chrome user and device settings page.

Remediation and Prevention

Google engineers were alerted to the outage via an internal monitoring alert on Wednesday, 06 March 2024 at 15:04 US/Pacific and immediately started an investigation. Once the nature and scope of the issue became clear, Google engineers initiated a rollback of the configuration change at 15:36 and the incident was fully resolved at 15:59 once the rollback completed.

Google is committed to preventing a repeat of this issue in the future and is completing the following actions:

  • Improve procedural documentation on how to safely cleanup access control settings from authorization configuration.
  • Complete thorough investigation of privilege usage for the Admin Console to prevent further issues of this type.
  • Identify and register a new owner for this privilege in the application manifest and create permission mapping for faster verification in the future.

Google is committed to quickly and continually improving our technology and operations to prevent service disruptions. We appreciate your patience and apologize again for the impact to your organization. We thank you for your business.

Detailed Description of Impact

On Wednesday, 06 March 2024 from 14:32 to 15:59 US/Pacific, Google Workspace users attempting to work within the Admin Console encountered an HTTP 500 error when accessing user or device setting pages within the console.

Affected products: Admin Console

Resolved - Between April 3rd, 2024 23:15 UTC and April 4th, 2024 01:10 UTC, GitHub Actions experienced a partial infrastructure outage that led to degraded workflows (failed or delayed starts). Additionally, 0.15% of Webhook deliveries were degraded due to an unrelated spike in database latency in a single availability zone. SLOs for Actions were 90% during the incident, but this was not evenly distributed across customers. We statused green after a long stretch of recovered SLOs, starting at April 4th, 2024 00:35 UTC. During this incident, we also had issues with incident tooling (https://www.githubstatus.com/) failing to update the public status page and occasionally not loading.
The incident was resolved after the infrastructure issue was mitigated at 2024-04-04 04:27 UTC.
We are working to improve monitoring and processes in response to this incident. We are investigating how we can improve resilience and our communication with our infrastructure provider, and how we can better handle ongoing incidents that are no longer impacting SLOs. We are also improving our incident tooling to ensure that the public status page is updated in a timely manner.

Issue Summary:
From April 4, 2024 at 12:30 PM PDT to April 4, 2024 at 10:20 PM PDT, some customers were receiving this error message when trying to rename a channel: “Oops/Whoops, something went wrong with renaming the channel. Please try again.”

We identified a code change which inadvertently altered the permission to edit channel. This resulted in this error being shown.

We rolled back this change, correcting the issue.

Impacted customers should no longer experience any further trouble after reloading their Slack.
To reload Slack use Command + Shift + R on Mac and Ctrl + Shift + R on Windows/Linux.

On April 2, 2024 from 2:50 PM PDT to 6:04 PM PDT, customers may have encountered missing messages in channels and conversations, as well as error messages in the Activity and Threads views. 

A code change inadvertently caused a rendering loop, preventing the Slack desktop client from correctly displaying some messages. We reverted the code change and rolled back to an earlier version, resolving the issue for all affected customers.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From 3:41 PM PDT until 4:13 PM PDT on April 1st, 2024, some customers experienced problems with the Slack interface, including issues with text color and contrast.

We made a code change to improve some of our CSS styling. This change inadvertently caused a problem with some color and contrast variables in dark mode, resulting in the interface issues.

As an immediate mitigation step, we stopped the code change from rolling out any further. We then reverted to an earlier version, resolving the issues for all affected customers.
articles.title: Incident: Incorrect font color and unexpected UI elements

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From March 31, 2024 at 6:30 AM PDT to March 31, 2024 at 11:50 AM PDT, some customers were unable to create a channel with a workflow.

We identified a backend code change that inadvertently changed some data, causing the "Create a channel" workflow step to hang in the Workflow Builder.

We rolled back the change, correcting the issue. Impacted customers should no longer be experiencing any further issues.
articles.title: Incident: Workflows configured using the Create a channel step may encounter an error on channel creation

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On March 28, 2024 at 10:47 AM PDT until 11:20 AM PDT, a small number of users experienced trouble using workflows, connecting or signing into Slack, and creating accounts.

A recent change to a database service that's responsible for processing user activity in Slack had an influx of unexpected traffic. This traffic caused an increased number of error rates and failures which prevented users from accessing certain features.

When our internal health tools alerted us of the influx of errors, we paused any further code changes in an effort to improve database processing.

During our investigation, it was discovered that as a result of the unexpected traffic, the database service automatically timed out after about 30 minutes. This timeout allowed the database to return to normal and process new requests without causing errors.

We moved forward with a continued period of investigation and monitored to ensure impact did not reoccur.
articles.title: Incident: Trouble signing in and degraded workflows

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On March 27, 2024 from 8:13 AM PDT until 3:38 PM PDT, some users experienced errors when attempting to login, send messages, open channels, or threads.

We traced this issue back to a subset of errors that occurred within a set of cross-functional databases that are responsible for basic user features in Slack. As an immediate step to mitigate the issue, we automatically performed a restore of the backups of these affected databases.

Once the process of restoring these backups was completed, the databases began successfully processing user requests, fully restoring the functionality of the affected features. We are working to put safeguards in place to reduce the likelihood of this issue occurring again in the future.
articles.title: Incident: Issues loading Slack for less than 1% of customers

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
From Monday March 18, 2024 at 9:07 PM PDT to Tuesday March 19, 2024 until 12:06 AM PDT, some users saw blurry image previews.

A change was made to a backend service that's responsible for the handling of files in workspaces that have International Data Residency (IDR) enabled. This change inadvertently affected the ability for Slack to correctly generate previews for image files. On Tuesday March 19 around 12:06 AM PDT, we reverted the change to stop any new files to be loaded with blurry image previews. 

Thereafter, we conducted an in-depth investigation to find any images that were uploaded during the impacted duration to correct its image clearness. On Wednesday March 20, 12:50 PM PDT, all images were restored. 

Thank you for bearing with us while we worked through this case.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with file previews

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
From Monday March 25, 2024 at 3:30 PM PDT to Tuesday March 26, 2024 until 8:51 AM PDT, some users saw the error message REB686069408 when adding Google Sheets to their workflows.

This was traced to a backend change related to how Workflow Builder searches for a Google Sheet when using the Google Sheets workflow step, but the user interface was not receiving proper label values causing the error. 

We reverted the change as an initial attempt to fix, but learned this didn't resolve the issue as we continued to see incorrect value data.

We corrected the problematic piece of code that allowed for the Google Sheets step to properly search for the spreadsheet using the correct search value. This restored the workflow step to full functionality.
articles.title: Incident: Users receiving error when adding Google Sheets step to workflows.

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
On Monday March 25, 2024 at 6:00 AM PDT to around 8:00 AM PDT, some users did not receive two-factor authentication (2FA) codes via SMS and couldn't log into Slack.

We determined this was caused by an issue with an upstream 2FA provider. We monitored communications from the provider and confirmed Slack users could successfully sign in once the upstream issue was resolved.
articles.title: Incident: Users not receiving 2FA codes

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On March 20, 2024 from around 8:05 AM PDT until 10:33 PM PDT, some users experienced various issues with Slack such as loading channel membership lists, joining a channel, setting or clearing their user statuses, loading profile images, incorrect huddle status, and inconsistent user states if a user was recently deactivated or reactivated.

A recent change to resolve an unrelated traffic issue we observed with our backend servers inadvertently caused connections to database caching services to timeout.

At around 12:00 PM PDT, we had identified the cause of the timeout failures and began gradually deploying a fix. We continued to closely monitor our health metrics for any abnormalities as our remediation progressed.

By 10:33 PM PDT, the deploy successfully reached all affected users, these users would have immediately received the fix through a hard refresh of their Slack client (Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + R). By 8:49 AM PDT on March 21, 2024, most affected users received the fix without a required hard refresh.

We are continuing to investigate this issue and implement preventative measures to reduce the likelihood of this occurring again in the future.
articles.title: Incident: Trouble loading channels, viewing channel membership, and clearing user status

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On March 19, 2024 from 2:50 PM PDT to 8:16 PM PDT, less than 1% of users were unable to load Slack. 

A corrupted table in our database infrastructure prevented one of our databases from responding to requests, causing connection issues for customers whose workspaces were hosted on that database. We manually triggered a backup of the affected database. While we always have backups in place, we were concerned that the existing replicas would be affected by the same bug. We used this manual backup to provision new databases, spinning up several fresh replicas. 

Once the replicas were up and running, we directed traffic from the impacted workspaces to these new databases. This restored access for affected customers. We continued working to address the bug that caused the original issue to prevent this from occurring to any other database.
articles.title: Incident: Issues loading Slack for less than 1% of customers

We identified the cause of the problem and manually increased the database capacity, restoring normal functionality for impacted users. 

Thank you for bearing with us while we resolved this issue.
